data.name: AudioOverlayParagraph1
data.value: Every dot is a real bus. Dozens of them, maybe more, moving through a city that never agreed on a grid. They follow Peachtree and Cascade and Memorial Drive, routes drawn around what Atlanta actually is rather than what a planner imagined.

data.name: AudioOverlayParagraph2
data.value: The harmony is slow and syncopated. A note lands where the bus happens to be along its route — deep in Vine City, crossing the connector, idling at Edgewood-Candler Park. Morning fills the piece with movement; after midnight the map goes quiet and the notes stretch out. What is playing right now has not played before.

data.name: AudioOverlayParagraph3
data.value: MARTA runs on faith. You wait, and then it comes. This is the music inside that waiting.

data.name: WmataAudioOverlayParagraph1
data.value: Every dot is a real bus or train. Hundreds of them, spread across a city that was planned on a diagonal and then grew past every boundary. They follow Wisconsin and Georgia and Benning Road, and the Red Line arcing through Bethesda, routes drawn around three jurisdictions that never quite agreed on anything.

data.name: WmataAudioOverlayParagraph2
data.value: The harmony shifts with the system. A note lands where the vehicle happens to be along its route — transferring at Metro Center, crossing the Anacostia, moving through Silver Spring at rush hour. Commuter peaks fill the piece with density; late nights thin it out to something sparse and unhurried. What is playing right now has not played before.

data.name: WmataAudioOverlayParagraph3
data.value: WMATA connects a capital to itself. Across DC, Maryland, and Virginia, something is always moving. This is the music inside that motion.

data.name: MbtaAudioOverlayParagraph1
data.value: Every dot is a real bus or train. Hundreds of them, spread across a region that grew outward from a harbor and never stopped. They follow Massachusetts Avenue and Blue Hill and the Riverside Line, routes drawn around Boston, Cambridge, Somerville, and the towns reaching out to Providence and Newburyport.

data.name: MbtaAudioOverlayParagraph2
data.value: The harmony follows the system. A note lands where the vehicle happens to be along its route — surfacing at Park Street, crossing the Charles, moving through Roxbury at rush hour. The Red, Orange, and Blue lines weave through the piece alongside hundreds of buses. What is playing right now has not played before.

data.name: MbtaAudioOverlayParagraph3
data.value: The T is the oldest subway in America. It carries the city forward on the same lines it always has. This is the music inside that motion.

data.name: MbtaOverlayParagraph1
data.value: Every dot is a real MBTA vehicle, pulled live and turned into sound. Buses and trains — including the Red, Orange, and Blue lines — move through Greater Boston in real time, and the map plays what they're doing right now.

data.name: InfoOverlayParagraph1
data.value: Every dot is a real MARTA vehicle, pulled live and turned into sound. Buses and trains move through Atlanta in real time, and the map plays what they're doing right now.

data.name: InfoOverlayParagraph2
data.value: Audio is required for the full experience — tap the volume button if you don't hear anything. Use the route filters to isolate routes and the layers button to toggle the city map.

data.name: InfoOverlayParagraph3
data.value: Built as a small experiment in turning a transit feed into generative music. Each note is placed by where a vehicle sits along its route, so what you hear is never quite the same twice.

data.name: WmataOverlayParagraph1
data.value: Every dot is a real WMATA vehicle, pulled live and turned into sound. Buses and Metro trains move through Washington DC, Maryland, and Virginia in real time, and the map plays what they're doing right now.
